title: The Gift of the Magi
text:
On Christmas Eve, Della Dillingham Young counted her money three times. One dollar and eighty seven cents, saved a penny at a time by bargaining with the grocer and the butcher. It was all she had to buy a present for her husband Jim, who earned twenty dollars a week. She flopped down on the shabby couch and cried.

The young couple had two treasures. One was Jim's gold watch, which had been his father's and his grandfather's. The other was Della's hair, long and shining, falling below her knees. Della put on her old brown jacket and hat and went to a shop that bought hair. She sold it for twenty dollars. Then she searched the stores and found the perfect gift: a simple platinum chain for Jim's watch. It cost twenty one dollars.

When Jim came home and saw her short curls, he stood frozen, staring. She begged him not to be angry; her hair would grow back. He drew a package from his coat. Inside was a set of beautiful tortoise shell combs, with jeweled rims, that she had longed for in a shop window for ages. She held them to her heart. Then she showed him the watch chain.

Jim lay down on the couch, put his hands behind his head and smiled. He had sold the watch to buy her combs.
lesson: The worth of a gift lies in what the giver was willing to give up. Couples who sacrifice for each other are already rich.
source: O. Henry, The Gift of the Magi (first published in the New York Sunday World, 1905)
